_meta.purpose: Versions whose Tier-1.C TAG-COLLISION check is waived in scripts/check-release-version.py (CI job build-and-test). Nothing else in the guard consults this file: shape, releases.json integrity and version-regression are unwaivable, and there is deliberately no env-var or commit-trailer bypass.
_meta.when_a_waiver_is_legitimate: Essentially never. A tag collision means the version has already been promoted, and the `release-tag-integrity` ruleset (id 20140435) forbids deleting or re-pointing v* / promote-v* tags — so the correct response is almost always to bump to the next free version with `node scripts/add-release.mjs <next> "<highlight>"`. Reach for a waiver only when a tag exists that provably never shipped (e.g. created by a dry run) and cannot be removed.
_meta.entry_shape: { version: '3.81.0', reason: 'why this collision is safe', date: 'YYYY-MM-DD', waived_by: 'name' }
_meta.note: `version` is the bare package.json version WITHOUT the leading 'v'.
_meta.source: Release-version guard, added 2026-07-31 after the v3.81.0 tag burn (package.json un-bumped at 3.80.0 on the promoted SHA 00558fe, forcing a second promote as v3.81.1).
